column1: # docs/pointer-groundtruth.tsv — THE LABELLED GROUND TRUTH for the bare-pointer class.
# WHAT THIS IS. Every `<token> in <target>` construction in paper-III.md and paper-IV.md at
# revision 07cd47e whose TARGET is BARE under wt160's named-target tests N1-N6 — 341 rows, of
# 444 constructions in all (282 here from Paper III, 59 from Paper IV). Those are REVIEW-028
# section 3's and section 6.4's numbers, reproduced row for row by scripts/wt166_pointer_groundtruth.py,
# which imports wt160's own _flatten, _target_window and _is_named rather than re-implementing them.
# WHY IT EXISTS. REVIEW-028 established that the count wt160 and wt163 return is a property of
# the VERB LIST. Its section 8 falsifier 5 named the one attack that could still rescue the
# enumeration — carve out a defensible sub-class of bare targets STRUCTURALLY, with no verb list —
# and observed that nobody had run it because nobody had the labels. Without labels there is no
# truth set, so no proposed detector can be scored at all. These are the labels.
# HOW IT WAS BUILT. All 341 rows were READ, in context, by wealthTensor-89. No verb list was
# consulted while labelling: a ground truth built with a word list cannot score a word list.
# The adjudication rule is REVIEW-028 section 3's, fixed before this reading and unchanged:
#   POINTER iff (a) the construction asserts that some content is LOCATED IN a document,
#   artefact, run or record — the reader is being asked to go there to check — AND (b) the
#   target as written carries no handle a reader could follow.
# Clause (b) holds for all 341 by construction, since N1-N6 are silent on every row. So the
# COLUMNS.  file · line · token · target · label · confidence · reason
#   (file, line, token, target) is the KEY. It is unique across all 341 rows and every component
#   is recomputed from 07cd47e, so the labels cannot drift from the corpus: wt166 REFUSES (exit 2)
#   if the recomputed key set differs from this file's by a single row.
#   `line` is the source line of the FLATTENED text's match, as wt160 reports it.
#   `confidence` is FIRM or SOFT. SOFT marks a row this session judges could defensibly go the
#   other way, and it is not decoration: wt166 scores every candidate test THREE times — against
#   the labels as written (PRIMARY, 15 pointers), against FIRM pointers only (STRICT, 11), and
#   against PRIMARY plus every SOFT NOT-POINTER (LOOSE, 51) — so no verdict in REVIEW-029 rests
#   on a judgement call. There are 36 SOFT NOT-POINTER rows.
# THE ONE ROW REVIEW-028 MISSED. `III 1261 are in the run logs` is a bare pointer under this rule
# and it is NOT among REVIEW-028 section 4's fourteen. Its verb is the COPULA. REVIEW-028's own
# vocabulary-free reading filtered the corpus's 264 tokens at step 2 by keeping "every token that
# could locate content in an artefact" — and `are` does not look like a locating verb even though
# it does the locating work. That is REVIEW-028 section 8 falsifier 1, fired, and it means the
# vocabulary-free reading had a covert vocabulary after all. See REVIEW-029 section 5.
# THE LABELS ARE AT 07cd47e AND DO NOT MOVE WHEN THE MANUSCRIPTS ARE REPAIRED. wt164 repaired
# four of these rows at HEAD and wt167 repairs a fifth; wt166 always reads 07cd47e, so a repair
# cannot silently invalidate the ground truth. That is deliberate.
